claude_proposed_widenings.name: passive_grant family for ClassFeatureMechanics
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Scholar is a permanent passive benefit granted at acquisition time. It has no activation cost, no use-count resource, and no rest-reset cadence. The existing 'activation' family requires all three and represents an on-demand action. Forcing Scholar into 'activation' with a free cost and fictitious use-count would produce a dishonest trace. A 'passive_grant' family (or equivalent) is needed to represent features that fire once and persist indefinitely.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: You have Expertise in the chosen skill.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: GrantExpertiseEffect (variant of ClassFeatureEffect)
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The effect is Expertise: double proficiency bonus on ability checks with the chosen skill. The v4 atom inventory contains 'grant_proficiency', but ClassFeatureEffect has no variant for it. A GrantExpertiseEffect (or GrantProficiencyEffect with an expertise flag) is required to express this effect in the surface type.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: You have Expertise in the chosen skill.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: ChoiceAtAcquisition for skill selection
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Scholar requires the player to choose one skill from a closed list at feature-acquisition time (Arcana, History, Investigation, Medicine, Nature, or Religion). The surface has no mechanism to express 'choose one from list at acquisition' for passive class features. This is a choice that precedes runtime and is locked in permanently. The closest prior art is Alarm's creature_exemption_list (chosenAtCast: true), but there is no analogous grammar for class feature acquisition-time choices.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: Choose one of the following skills in which you have proficiency: Arcana, History, Investigation, Medicine, Nature, or Religion.
